programmes.d: TV star and stand-up comic Paul Reiser tells Johnny what he says to people, so they’ll think he’s listening to them when he really isn’t.
Famed comedian Richard Pryor pokes fun at his failure at marriage and reflects on his new sobriety. Fellow guest and The Breakfast Club star Ally Sheedy describes life as a senior at USC.

Would you believe Don Adams guest stars? Don plays a talk show host beset with technical difficulties, Carol's agitated husband in "The Lost Purse," and (with Harvey) one of a pair of griping fathers.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents The Supremes, The Alcettys, Frank Ifield, Roberta Peters, and Holiday on Ice.
John Lithgow and Buddy Hackett stop by the couch, plus Johnny talks about the Christmas season.
Andy Griffith and Barbara McNair join Carol and the gang tonight! Sketches include a football coach who can't help but bring his work home with him, and a production number about Smokey The Bear.
Guest star Michele Lee headlines a wintry and wonderful production number in this episode, which also offers another visit with the 10th Street Family.
Guest stars Michele Lee and Flip Wilson respectively dazzle with song and stand-up comedy, and Carol vamps in "V.I.P." as Hollywood sex symbol Mae East.
Tonight's episode features a pair of fan favorite recurring sketches. First, "The Family" steps out as Mama, Eunice, and Ed go to a fancy restaurant, and Tim's "Oldest Man" is a Wild West sheriff.
Good evening...tonight, guest stars Rich Little and Eydie Gorme join in a tribute to Alfred Hitchcock! Also: Carol and Harvey play a couple not speaking to each other in a largely pantomimed sketch.

programmes.t: The Best of the Dean Martin Show
programmes.d: Sketches and songs with Dean Martin and celebrity guests Jonathan Winters, Paul Lynde, and Norm Crosby.
Danny DeVito appears on the couch, as well as Rohan Varavadekar and Calvin Trillin.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Chakiris joins Carol for the Q&A, while the latest 'Carol & Sis' sketch finds Jones playing Roger's temp secretary--much to Carol's dismay.

programmes.t: Comedy Legends from The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Dick Gregory's "Politics, Americans, Economics, Sports"; Shelley Berman's "Father, Teenage Daughter, Sex"; Nipsey Russell's "New York City"; Sid Caesar and Betsy Palmer's "New Parents"
Television icons Phil Silvers (Sgt. Bilko) and Jean Stapleton (Edith Bunker) guest star! Sketches include "The Old Folks", commercial parodies, and a musical number by Carol in the style of Cher.
Garry Moore and Durward Kirby team up with Carol and the gang for the evening, appearing in the sketch "Science Fiction Playhouse." Meanwhile, "Carol & Sis" features Carol three sheets to the wind.
Lucille Ball and Mel Torme lend their tremendous talents to a spoof of the classic comedy "Some Like It Hot" with a gender-flipping twist: Lucy and Carol in the Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon roles!
Another batch of kitchen commercials highlights this episode, while Tim returns as the steelworker looking to do away with annoying wife Carol.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: The Pointer Sisters join Carol in a rockin' musical spoof of 'Cinderella' in tonight's episode, which also features another round of commercial spoofs

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents Diana Ross and The Supremes, Spanky and Our Gang, Charlie Cairoli and Company, Franco Corelli, The Muppets, and George Carlin.
Carol and the gang take their act across the pond for this special episode filmed in London! Have a cuppa and enjoy the intercontinental champions of comedy at their finest.
12-year-old TV star Ricky Schroder (Silver Spoons) shows off his skill juggling plastic eggs. Then Johnny gives it a try, unaware that Ricky swapped the plastic ones for real eggs. What a mess!
One of the world’s most influential journalists, Barbara Walters describes dealing with touchy heads of state and getting Christmas cards from world leaders.
Sex expert Dr. Ruth Westheimer talks about her new book, Dr. Ruth’s Guide for the Sexually Perplexed, and shares some of the funniest questions she gets asked.
It's a fear-themed episode as Rosanna Arquette discusses her phobia of critics, plus Oprah Winfrey and Alan Thicke also reveal their fears.
Sean Connery gives a Bond trivia quiz and recalls his scariest stunts. Comic Keenan Ivory Wayans says dating white girls is like being on Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom; people can’t stop staring.
Carol's guests are Mickey Rooney and John Davidson! Davidson sings "Somewhere", Rooney takes part in a wild, wild Western, and Carol must choose between the two (and Lyle) on "The Rat Race."
Did you know Bob Newhart started his career as an accountant? We're glad he switched to comedy and visited Johnny for this episode, which also features James Stephens and Ronnie Porter.

Remember The Thorn Birds? Meet Colleen McCullough, who wrote the blockbuster novel-turned-mini series. Lou Brock discusses his base-stealing record and acting legend Eli Wallach chats about his craft. Don Rickles plugs his show C.P.O. Sharkey.

Vincent Price is a thriller of a guest star in a salute to horror films. Meanwhile, George imagines himself as a riverboat gambler--but still can't escape Zelda; and a pregnant pause on "Carol & Sis."
Guest Gloria Swanson arrives for the Q&A...but she only has eyes for Lyle. Sketches include a "Carol & Sis" where the Bradfords try to discourage an elevator operator... who only has eyes for Carol.
Comic genius Carl Reiner makes his 46th visit to Johnny’s couch. Discusses his attempts at dieting and presents Johnny with a bunch of gifts: slippers, pipe, glasses, and….a gun.
Please welcome guests William Conrad and Isabel Sanford to the stage! A series of short television spoofs highlight this fast-paced episode, which also features another installment of "Carol & Sis."
Steve Lawrence and the ever-popular Tim Conway guest star! Steve plays a talk show host, and then solves a mystery as Detective Cobumble in a TV spoof featuring Tim as a butler.
Martha Raye and Betty Grable guest in the soap opera spoof "As The Stomach Turns." And a "Beautiful Legs" contest reveals stiff completion from an unlikely competitor. All this, and Carol's Q&A too!
The gorgeous and talented Ann-Margret says she disguises herself in a black wig when out in public. Screen legend Robert Mitchem reveals he did time on a chain gang, at age 15.
Roddy McDowall guest stars. Sketches include: Harvey's proposal to Carol is stymied by an outbreak of infectious laughter; Roddy and Carol working an assembly line; a spoof of "The Little Foxes."
